exposure: gestational age at birth (early term vs. full term)
mode of delivery (caesarean section vs. vaginal delivery)
outcome: Lung function at 8-9 years and 14-17 years
cohort: 14,062 Caucasian, singleton, term births from the Avon Longitudinal Study of Parents and Children
finding: While early-term-born children had lower lung function values at 8-9 years compared to full-term-born children, their lung function was similar by 14-17 years of age.
mod_finding: Delivery by caesarean section did not influence later spirometry, and the effect of early-term birth was not modified by delivery by caesarean section.
